Yes, that's the right persistence boundary. The things that are actually *mine* — every saved bookmark, my edits, notes, labels, what's marked read-later, and the sort order I chose — should all still be there when I come back; losing any of that would defeat the whole purpose of saving. But the momentary stuff, like a search I was typing, a label I'd filtered to, or a note I'd expanded, is just where I happened to be in that session, so it makes sense for the app to reopen on my full collection with a clean slate. That's exactly the line I'd draw between "my data" and "where I was looking." Good.

Setting my default sort once and having it stick is a nice touch, too — that's the kind of personal preference I'd expect to be remembered.
